finding: The live range of $1,075-$3,700 starts too low and tops out a little low for trucks. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $1,617-$3,301 (11.5-18.8 hr); midsize 2016 Camry about $1,704-$3,044 (11.5-17.0 hr); truck 2012 F-150 5.0L, both heads, about $2,842-$4,349 (20.9-24.2 hr); luxury 2016 Cadillac Escalade 6.2L, both heads, about $1,358-$2,157 (9.9-11.1 hr). The lowest total we can build is about $1,360, and that pairs a manufacturer warranty time on a pushrod V8 with an online gasket-and-bolt set that leaves out the intake, exhaust and valve cover gaskets, with no machine-shop work, coolant, oil or air-conditioning service, so real quotes start higher; nothing supports $1,075. At the top, both heads on a full-size truck with overhead cams come to about $4,350, above $3,700. A range of roughly $1,400-$4,400 fits the evidence better. RepairPal ($2,572-$3,386 national; F-150 $3,474-$4,603) and CarParts.com ($2,400-$3,200) sit inside our built totals; only a 2023 J.D. Power article ($1,000-$3,000) supports the live low end. How solid the labor times are: only the luxury low end is a manufacturer time for the example vehicle. The economy and midsize low ends are Honda warranty flat-rate times for comparable cars (11.5 hr for the 2016-17 Civic 1.5L turbo and for the 2018-22 Accord 1.5L turbo; other Honda bulletins give 10.8-12.4 hr), not Toyota times. The economy high end (18.8 hr) is a technician forum post quoting a labor guide for the sister 1.8L engine in a Prius, and the midsize high end (17 hr) is a parts retailer's statement about Camrys with no model years given; both are weak. The truck times are Ford warranty times for replacing both cylinder heads on an F-150 with the 2.7L V6 (20.9-24.2 hr), not the 5.0L V8; a technician forum post puts the 5.0L book time at about 24 hours, which agrees. Luxury: the example was changed from a 2015 BMW 328i to a 2016 Cadillac Escalade because three attempts found no stated head gasket time for the BMW (its bulletins point to BMW's own labor-time system). The Escalade low end (9.9 hr, both heads) is GM's own warranty time for that vehicle; the high end (11.1 hr) is an Acura warranty time for a 2025-26 ADX four-cylinder, a comparable luxury-brand vehicle and not the example. Both are warranty times, so the luxury total is a floor, and it should not be read as the price for a European luxury car: no stated time was found for one, and overhead-cam turbo engines generally take longer than this pushrod V8 (GM allows 14.3 hr for the same engine in a Corvette). Other caveats: the midsize parts figure is a single aftermarket set price without head bolts; the truck bolt-set listing does not say whether it covers both heads; the luxury high parts figure prices 19 of the 20 head bolts; fluids were not priced.
extras: Machine-shop work is the biggest add-on: the head is normally checked for flatness and cracks and resurfaced, and a warped or cracked head means more machining or a replacement head. Quotes also commonly add coolant, engine oil and filter, thermostat, spark plugs, a diagnosis fee (cooling-system pressure test or combustion-gas test), shop supplies and sales tax. Many shops recommend doing the timing chain or belt, water pump and related seals while the engine is apart, and V engines may be quoted for one head or both, so check which the quote covers.
